title: Church authority does not remove the same inquisitive doubts
source_text: XXII. Tertio, istud argumentum supponit dubitationes illas quas adversus Scripturam movere potest humana ratio per Ecclesiae authoritatem tolli. Sed hoc quoque falsum est. Nam quaerenti unde scimus libros qui circumferuntur Apostolorum & Prophetarum esse, aut omnino fuisse Apostolos & Prophetas ullos, non satis fit dicendo Ecclesiam ita dicere & docere. Siquidem pari jure quaeret ille unde scimus Ecclesiam verum dicere, & duci a Spiritu sancto. At cum tot sint sectae inter Christianos, unde scimus hanc potius quam illam esse veram Ecclesiam, aut ullam omnino esse in terris Dei Ecclesiam. Certe tum ipsis nihil supererit quo se adversus ejusmodi percunctatorem tueantur, nisi notae & praejudicia illa quibus Ecclesiae Romanae authoritas ipsorum judicio redditur credibilis. Verum hic non quaeruntur ejusmodi argumenta, sed quae certo probent rem esse de fide, & quibus fides tanquam suo fundamento niti possit. Ac praeterea, si istuc deveniendum foret, promptum est nobis ostendere Scripturae authoritatem longe pluribus & certioribus argumentis & notis commendari, quam cujuscunque inter Christianos Ecclesiae authoritatem.
pass_a_gloss: Third, that argument supposes that those doubts which human reason can move against Scripture are removed by the Church's authority. But this also is false. For to one asking whence we know that the books which circulate are of the Apostles and Prophets, or that there were Apostles and Prophets at all, it is not enough to say that the Church so says and teaches. Since with equal right he will ask whence we know that the Church speaks truth and is led by the Holy Spirit. But when there are so many sects among Christians, whence do we know that this rather than that is the true Church, or that there is any Church of God on earth at all? Certainly then nothing will remain for them by which to defend themselves against such an inquirer, except those marks and prejudices by which the authority of the Roman Church is rendered credible in their judgment. But here such arguments are not sought, but ones that certainly prove the matter to be of faith, and on which faith can rest as on its foundation. And besides, if one had to come to that point, it is ready for us to show that Scripture's authority is recommended by far more and more certain arguments and marks than the authority of any Church among Christians.
pass_b_english: Third, the argument assumes that doubts human reason can raise against Scripture are cleared by the Church's authority. That too is false.

To someone asking how we know circulating books are the Apostles' and Prophets', or that there ever were Apostles and Prophets, it is not enough to say the Church so teaches — he will ask with equal right how we know the Church speaks truth and is led by the Spirit.

With so many Christian sects, how do we know this rather than that is the true Church — or that any Church of God is on earth at all? Then they have nothing left against such an inquirer but those marks and prejudices that make Rome's authority look credible to them.

But what we need here is not that kind of probability — it is what proves the matter to be of faith and can bear faith as its foundation. And if we did have to go there, we are ready to show that Scripture's authority is recommended by far more and surer arguments and marks than any Christian church's.
